beats.headline: Fangs, the robot
beats.text: Pre-production meeting, final seat. The representative introduces himself in a robotic voice as Warlord Fangs of the Reavers: a square-headed, old-school robot vibrating up and down as if powered by a diesel engine, straight out of a sixties science fiction film. Crawler Carl knows from the Cookbook that the look is for his benefit, and that Reavers can switch shape whenever they like. Crawler Donut asks whether his name is really Fangs, and whether he is a robot vampire or, better, a werewolf robot. Cascadia snaps at her. Before anyone answers, the Viceroy beside him loses his head.

beats.headline: His personal defense deployment
beats.text: A note from me about the paratroopers who came down through the Posse's protections. Most of the people who sign on as Reaver soldiers were hungry and without direction when they walked into the recruiter's office. That is not to say you should feel sorry for these ones. These are all members of Warlord Fang's personal defense deployment. Rule of thumb: more than two or three cybernetics installed means they have voluntarily re-upped at least once. You get one free upgrade a deployment, or more if something gets shot off.

beats.headline: A different body at the council
beats.text: Warlord council. Warlord Fang appears beside Ferdinand, no longer an old-school robot but a slight, wide-eyed human male of perhaps twenty, skin a little too pink, in a spotless white t-shirt and underwear. The only tell is the line of flashing lights at his temple. When Juice Box changes into a tall black armless thing with tentacles, and the table recoils, Warlord Fang inches away from it.

beats.headline: Not in his castle
beats.text: By the time the Nest tower is stabilised, it is clear Warlord Fang is not in the Reaver castle. The castle is abandoned except for its security system, which is a bunch of robots, and a gravity-magic dragon circling overhead. Crawler Carl casts Ping and finds both remaining Bloc warlords, Epitome Tagg and Warlord Fang, inside the rolling ball of bodies. Rosetta is blunt about it: Fang especially is difficult to locate, worse than a changeling.

beats.headline: Marked, and gone
beats.text: After Crawler Donut's spell breaks the ball, Warlord Fang is not among the dead. Crawler Carl is fairly sure Li Na marked both Tagg and Fang with the Ring of Divine Suffering, and neither has died, which means she cannot heal until they are. Britney reports Li Na tearing through the castle, glowing and silent, and the war mages gone through a portal. Carl guesses Li Na is hunting Tagg and Fang.

beats.headline: The least known of them
beats.text: Crawler Carl's working file on the subject, compiled on the way to the Reaver castle. Of all the warlords, Warlord Fang is the one least known. He is something like ninety-nine percent cybernetic and changes shape like a Terminator-style changeling. He and Tagg are probably the two richest warlords here. If he dies, it is no huge deal for the Reaver corporation: a physical chunk of his brain, called the Initial, is kept on one of their worlds, and every year they peel microscopic parts off it to build new citizens.

beats.headline: Inside the dragon
beats.text: For the record. The drake circling the Reaver castle is Calliope, Cybernetic Bleached Drake, level 130, a pet of Warlord Fang. Crawler Carl sets off the No Disassembles left inside by a wraith-possessed Louis, and the castle goes up. Calliope spirals out of the sky and bursts beside the rescue team. Warlord Fang has fallen. Credit goes to Warlord Carl, fifty-one percent, with one to Louis, forty to Juice Box, and the rest to Fang for hiding in the worst possible place, which was inside the dragon. The Reavers have been defeated.
